newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds reversed small opening losses to show modest gains at the close, hitching a lift with bund futures as the December contract set a new high.
The benchmark January 2006 Dutch government bond closed at 101.84/92 for a bid yield of 5.73 percent, compared with a close of 101.77/87 and 5.74 percent on Friday.

With long yields at their lowest for almost three years, dealers said investors were mainly shunning state issues, though some recent non-state issues, such as the ABN AMRO 6.25 pct 2006 and the Oce van der Grinten 6.375 pct 2006, found favour.
"Investors just don't seem interested in state bonds at these levels, though we might see them come back if yields drift back towards 5.80 or 5.90 percent," said one dealer.

Some dealers felt that surplus liquidity which still had to be invested might sustain further price gains for longer dated bonds up to the end of the year. But they saw little scope for yields to decline at the short end of the curve.
"Various Bundesbank members have said the (German) repo rate won't go any lower than three percent, so it's difficult to see how yields could come down at the short end," said one.
